newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish biker killed in drive-by shooting.
newsitem.headline: Danish biker killed in drive-by shooting.

text.p: Gunmen in the Danish town of Aalborg shot dead a member of the Hells Angels motorcycle gang overnight, bringing to eight the toll of dead in a three-year Nordic biker war, police said on Saturday.

Police in the small town, in the north of the Jutland peninsula, said that 26-year-old Kim Svendsen was driving in the town's eastern suburbs when another vehicle pulled alongside and an occupant fired at Svendsen, killing him and wounding a passenger, Lars Nielsen, 26.
Police raided the homes of known members of the rival Bandidos gang in the area and said they had detained 14 for questioning.

They suspected that the killing may have been a response to the December shooting in Aalborg of a Bandidos member who was seriously wounded as he sat in a car in the town centre by shots fired from a passing vehicle.
A 23-year-old man with ties to the Hells Angels was later jailed for the attack.
The two gangs, both offshoots of U.S. bike clans, have been battling over turf in Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden since shortly after the Bandidos established themselves in the region in 1993.
